lesson_body:
Welcome to our exciting journey into the world of shapes and spaces! Today, we will dive into the fascinating realm of geometry as we explore different types of shapes around us. Shapes are all around us, from the wheels on your bike to the windows in your house. Understanding shapes helps us make sense of the world! 

Let's start by identifying some basic shapes: circle, square, triangle, and rectangle. A circle is round and has no corners. A square has four equal sides and four corners – just like the boxes we use! A triangle has three sides and three corners, while a rectangle has two pairs of equal sides and also four corners. Together, these shapes form the building blocks of many objects we interact with every day. To illustrate these shapes, let’s look at some visual aids. 

Next, we will engage in an interactive discussion about where we can find these shapes in our environment. Can you think of any objects that are shaped like a triangle? Perhaps a slice of pizza? What about something that looks like a square? A book could be a great example! We will take a walk around the classroom to spot these shapes in real life, reinforcing their names and characteristics through first-hand experience. 

After our shape hunt, we will create our own shape collage! Using various colored paper cutouts of circles, squares, triangles, and rectangles, you will arrange them on a sheet of paper to create your own unique piece of art. This will not only help you remember the shapes but also allow you to get creative as we discuss how these shapes can combine to form new ones, like a house made of squares and triangles! Let’s have fun while learning about shapes and the spaces they occupy today!
interactive_assignment: For your hands-on activity, you will conduct a 'Shape Scavenger Hunt' in the classroom! You will receive a shape sheet that lists the four main shapes we covered: circle, square, triangle, and rectangle. Your task is to find at least one object in our room that matches each shape and draw a picture of it on your sheet. For example, if you find a circular clock, draw the clock next to the circle. After our hunt, we will gather as a class and share what we discovered. Don't forget to look carefully and think creatively when spotting your shapes!
